title: Intent
description: Work bigger than one Spec: what a person wants, in their words, with its outcome, and its slices grouped into phases. A person agrees to it before Specify starts on a slice, and each slice becomes a Spec when its work starts. The team writes it from a request, the person's own words. Aliases: Theme, Program.

title.description: One line. The language in the project's AGENTS.md may apply.

outcome.description: One sentence of what will be true once the Intent is done. The measures that say so are its `success_criteria`.

serves.description: The one item of the product scope this Intent serves: a product outcome or a standing outcome (`Outcome-n`), or a requirement (`Requirement-n`) of a BRD when there is no PRD and no standing outcomes. Never an objective: it is served through the outcome or requirement that serves it. Once a product scope exists, `aidd validate` errors on an Intent with none, and on an id that is missing, retired, or of the wrong kind.

success_criteria.description: How a person will know the outcome was reached: one measure for each criterion, each with its own day to read it. Required with `serves`. A criterion is a line under its Intent, not a work item: it has no status of its own, and its address (`INTENT-1#S1`) names it in `from`.

request.description: The request it answers, the person's own words: a path, such as `BRIEF.md` or a saved chat request, `specs/requests/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<slug>.md`, or a link. aidd never changes it.

from.description: What raised this Intent: an item id, a criterion's address (`INTENT-1#S1`), `band:<id>`, or a link. Leave it out when a person asked for the work. An Intent that a proposal raised names the proposal in `proposal` or here, never in both.

status.description: Only a person closes an Intent, because only a person can say its goal is met or dropped: they set `done`, or `cancelled` to stop it. Draft, approved, and active are derived from the approval and the slices. `approved` has no stored form, because nothing a person writes sets it: `approval` and the commit that holds it do, and a file that says `status: approved` is refused.

approval.description: A person's yes to the Intent: `{by, at}`, set by `aidd approve <id>`, never an agent. It holds only by its commit, as the common schema's `decision` says. A change to the Intent after it, apart from the fields an agent keeps current, such as `blocked_by` and a slice's `merged_in`, warns until they approve again.

waiting_on.description: Role, person, or interface the Intent waits on. While `waiting_on` names one, the Intent is blocked: `aidd status` shows it as a flag, not a status.

blocked_by.description: The work items this Intent waits for before its work starts, by id: no Spec under it starts until they finish. `aidd validate` checks that they form no cycle.

development_team.description: The development team accountable for the outcome: a key of the config's `development_teams`, which `aidd validate` checks. Its Specs are the team's work too. A slice may name another team in its own `development_team`.

trace_id.description: Joins this Intent with the Specs of other repositories that deliver its slices: each sets `trace_id: <home>-<Intent id>`.

reaches.description: How the work reaches users, agreed with the Intent. `incremental` (the default): each Spec merges by itself. `flagged`: each merges behind a flag that stays off until the last slice of the last phase, whose Merge approval is the launch, which a person always decides. `batched`: the Specs build on `intent/<ID>`, which one Merge approval merges.

covers.description: The ids of the proposal needs this Intent delivers, when it came from an accepted proposal.

proposal.description: The accepted proposal this Intent delivers, so every change under it traces back to what was promised.

start_on.description: The day a person chose for the work to start.

go_no_go.description: A person's decision to pursue the Intent or not, in the proposal's shape; `no_go` derives `cancelled`. Never an agent's.

phases.description: The phases, in order, each an ordered group of slices. An Intent with one phase lists that one.

tracker.description: The tracker's records this Intent links to, such as `{type: epic, id: PORT-31}`. aidd calls no tracker.

risks.description: The R of the RAID log, copied from the accepted proposal and kept current here.

assumptions.description: The A of the RAID log, copied from the accepted proposal and kept current here.

issues.description: The I of the RAID log, copied from the accepted proposal and kept current here.

dependencies.description: The D of the RAID log, copied from the accepted proposal and kept current here.

decisions.description: The scope decisions log, copied from the accepted proposal and kept current here. Each entry is a person's decision.

criterion.description: One way to know the outcome was reached, and when to read it.

measure_after_days.description: The days after the last release of the Intent's work, where users are, when the measure is read. Its day is read from that release, never stored.

measure_on.description: A day a person chose to read the measure. It wins over `measure_after_days`, unless it is earlier than the last release, and then aidd ignores it.

criterion_result.description: What the measure read, and what a person decided from it. The agent drafts it on the criterion's day from the metric's source, and a person approves it. A decision to retire the criterion is the one result that needs no number.

approval.description: A person's yes to this result.
